project.name: Group03
project.description: CSCI 3130 Group 03 marketplace with a Django 5.2 / Django REST Framework backend and a React 19 + Vite frontend, covering accounts, security and RBAC, seller applications, listings and catalog, image uploads, and search/discovery. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: authorize_listing_action

nodes.name: _authorize_remove

nodes.name: _authorize_purchase

nodes.name: ListingAction

nodes.name: DecisionCode

nodes.name: AuthorizationDecision

nodes.name: .gitlab-ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitLab CI pipeline with two sequential stages, test then build, where every job is interruptible (default: interruptible: true) so newer pushes cancel stale runs. Test stage: 'backend:test' runs on python:3.12-slim, installs backend/requirements.txt with a pip cache (.cache/pip, key python-dependencies), then runs 'python manage.py test --settings=config.test_settings' from backend/ to execute the Django/DRF test suite; 'frontend:test' runs on node:22-alpine, does 'npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline' in frontend/ (npm cache keyed on frontend/package-lock.json) and runs Vitest once via 'npm test -- --run'. Build stage (only after both test jobs pass): 'backend:build' byte-compiles the backend with 'python -m compileall -q backend' and packages it (excluding __pycache__, *.pyc, pytest/ruff caches and db.sqlite3) into the artifact backend-dist/backend-${CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA}.tar.gz; 'frontend:build' reinstalls dependencies and runs 'npm run build' (Vite) publishing frontend/dist/. Both build artifacts expire after 1 week. There is no deploy stage.
nodes.languageNotes: GitLab CI runs jobs in the same stage in parallel and stages sequentially; cache keys based on 'files:' (package-lock.json) invalidate the npm cache only when the lockfile changes, and ${CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA} is a predefined variable used to version artifacts.

It loads the React plugin, runs tests in a jsdom environment, enables globals so Testing Library auto-cleans between tests, runs src/tests/setup.js before every test file, and disables CSS processing.
nodes.languageNotes: Because vitest.config.js exists, Vitest ignores vite.config.js entirely, so the /api dev proxy is not active during tests; API calls must be mocked.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README, which lays out the Group 03 marketplace release by release and explains backend/frontend setup, the required .env variables, seeding commands, and how to run tests. The supporting document and deployment runbook add design decisions and the course VM workflow (MySQL DEVINT/TEST databases, starting Django and Vite). Together they give you the map for the rest of the tour: a Django REST backend and a React single-page frontend.

tour.title: Backend Entry and Settings
tour.description: manage.py is the Django command-line entry point: it points DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE at config.settings and dispatches commands like runserver, migrate, and test. settings.py loads backend/.env and refuses to start without DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and the database credentials, while config/__init__.py swaps in the pure-Python PyMySQL driver. The .env.example template shows exactly which secrets and SMTP settings a developer must provide.
tour.languageLesson: Django settings are a plain Python module. Reading required values with os.environ['KEY'] (instead of .get) makes misconfiguration fail fast with a KeyError at startup rather than at the first request.

tour.title: URL Routing Map
tour.description: The root urls.py mounts the admin site and every app's API under /api/, so it is the best index of the backend's features: auth, registration, rbac, seller applications, profiles, catalog, and listings. Each app owns its own urls.py; the security_core routes shown here expose the /api/auth/ endpoints for login, the 2FA step, logout, and the current-user payload that the frontend relies on.
tour.languageLesson: Django composes routing with include(): the project URLconf delegates path prefixes to per-app URLconfs, keeping each app self-contained and reusable.

tour.title: Security Core and 2FA
tour.description: security_core is the foundation that most other apps depend on: its models (an immutable AuditRecord, login failures, rate-limit locks, sessions, and 2FA devices) are among the most-imported files in the project. The views implement rate-limited email login with a TOTP second-factor step, while the two_factor and audit services provide reusable building blocks. Note the design choice that audit records cannot be updated or deleted, enforced through a custom QuerySet and manager.
tour.languageLesson: A custom Django QuerySet/Manager can override update() and delete() to raise errors, turning a model into an append-only log at the ORM level.

tour.title: Registration and Passwords
tour.description: Building on the security models, the registration app atomically creates a user, their email-verification status, and the default Buyer role, then issues single-use verification and email-change tokens. The password_policy module defines the mandatory rules (at least 6 characters, a digit, and a special character) as a Django password validator, so the same policy applies everywhere. Views stay thin and delegate to registration/services.py.
tour.languageLesson: transaction.atomic() wraps several ORM writes so they commit or roll back together, preventing half-created accounts.

tour.title: Role-Based Access Control
tour.description: rbac/services.py is the most depended-upon file in the graph: role and permission lookups, role assignment, and account suspension/reactivation all go through it, including protection of the last active administrator. The models define Role, Permission, their join tables, and per-user AccountState, and a data migration seeds the five marketplace roles and their permission matrix. HasRBACPermission then plugs these rules into DRF views.
tour.languageLesson: DRF permission classes implement has_permission/has_object_permission; listing them in a view's permission_classes keeps authorization declarative and out of the handler body.

tour.title: Seller Applications
tour.description: A Buyer becomes a Seller through an application: services.py validates submissions (including sniffing ID images and enforcing a 168-hour reapply cooldown) and handles moderator approval or refusal, granting the Seller role via RBAC. ID documents live in private, non-public storage and are only streamed to authorized users. listing_policy.py is the single source of truth for how a seller's suspension hides and freezes their listings, as recorded in the suspension decision document.

tour.title: Category Catalog
tour.description: Before listings can be published, they must sit in a leaf of the seeded category tree. seed.py hard-codes CATEGORY_TREE with typed attributes and a data migration loads it, while catalog/services.py validates a listing's category and attribute values. authorization.py centralizes who may publish, edit, remove, view, or purchase a listing by combining RBAC suspension state with seller eligibility from the previous step.
tour.languageLesson: Django data migrations (RunPython) seed reference data using historical models from apps.get_model, so the seed stays correct even as the live models evolve.

tour.title: Listings Model and Lifecycle
tour.description: Listings are the heart of the marketplace and are never physically deleted. states.py holds the single table of allowed transitions (Draft, Active, Paused, Sold out, Ended, Removed), and every change goes through change_state and an append-only ListingStateChange history. lifecycle.py adds owner pause/resume/end actions and automatic Sold out/Ended transitions, as specified in docs/lifecycle.md.

tour.title: Listings API and Search
tour.description: The listings views are thin: they delegate persistence to services.py, which authorizes every create, update, publish, and remove through the catalog policy from Step 8. validation.py checks field formats on every save and completeness at publish time, and search.py runs case-insensitive phrase matching over purchasable listings combined with catalog, currency, and price filters. docs/search.md documents this contract.

tour.title: Frontend Shell and API Client
tour.description: On the React side, main.jsx mounts <App /> in StrictMode, and App.jsx parses hash-based routes, loads the session from /api/auth/me/, and renders the matching screen. Every request goes through api.js, which ensures a CSRF cookie exists and attaches the X-CSRFToken header so Django's session authentication works. vite.config.js proxies /api to the Django dev server, so frontend and backend share an origin in development.
tour.languageLesson: React hooks such as useEffect load data after render (e.g. fetching the session once on mount), while useState drives re-rendering when the response arrives.

tour.title: Frontend Account Features
tour.description: These screens are the UI for Steps 4-7: AuthForms handles login with the 2FA challenge and recovery codes, Registration validates passwords client-side with rules mirroring the backend policy, and TwoFactorSettings manages TOTP setup. SellerApplication lets a buyer apply to sell, and RoleManagement gives administrators account search, role assignment, and suspension.

tour.title: Frontend Listings and Search
tour.description: listingsApi.js is the single client module for the listings and catalog APIs, converting snake_case payloads into camelCase objects for the components. ListingCatalog keeps search state in the URL hash (via searchParams.js) and calls the search endpoint from Step 10, while ListingForm gives sellers a leaf-category picker with dynamic attribute inputs and client-side validation.

tour.title: Testing and GitLab CI
tour.description: The GitLab CI pipeline runs two sequential stages, test then build, with interruptible jobs so newer pushes cancel stale runs. Backend tests run via manage.py test with config.test_settings, which supplies placeholder database credentials and a test secret key, and suites like listings/tests/test_api.py exercise the endpoints over HTTP. Frontend tests run with Vitest using vitest.config.js and a setup file that registers jest-dom matchers, as in the Registration.test.jsx suite.
tour.languageLesson: In GitLab CI YAML, stages run in order while jobs in the same stage run in parallel; 'interruptible: true' lets GitLab auto-cancel redundant pipelines. Separate test settings let CI run without production secrets.

tour.title: Frontend Test Example
tour.description: To round out testing, Registration.test.jsx shows the frontend style: Vitest with Testing Library renders the form, checks that weak passwords are blocked without calling the API, and verifies submission. The ListingRoutes suite renders App with a mocked session to confirm hash routes and access rules for sellers, guests, and non-sellers, complementing the backend suites from the previous step.
tour.languageLesson: Testing Library encourages querying by role and label (getByRole, getByLabelText) so tests assert on what users see rather than implementation details; vi.mock replaces modules like the API client.
